subject.title: Cron consecutiveErrors increments on gateway-restart interruptions, masking real agent-failure rate (post-#50414)

question: Should gateway-restart recovery reuse the existing `skipped` cron outcome, or introduce a public `interrupted` outcome for work that stopped before producing an agent result?
rationale: Both choices change durable cron semantics consumed by health reporting, delivery, retry/backoff, and operator tooling; source evidence establishes the bug but cannot select the permanent status contract.

options.title: Reuse `skipped` for restart interruptions
options.body: Keep the diagnostic reason but avoid a new public status, leave error and skipped counters unchanged, and suppress failure delivery for recovered interrupted runs.

options.title: Add `interrupted` as a terminal status
options.body: Expose the distinction explicitly, but define and document its compatibility, retry, health, delivery, and API behavior before implementation.

recommendation.title: Reuse `skipped` for restart interruptions
recommendation.body: Keep the diagnostic reason but avoid a new public status, leave error and skipped counters unchanged, and suppress failure delivery for recovered interrupted runs.

likelyOwner.reason: Their active adjacent restart-recovery work is the closest identified code-path context, though current-main history ownership still needs confirmation.
